name: The Content Engine: 12 Prompts for Solo Founders
tagline: Turn a single business insight into an entire week of targeted social content.
metaDescription: Transform one core insight into a week of high-converting social posts. 12 plug-and-play AI prompts built specifically for time-strapped solo founders.
description:
Building a company leaves almost no time for consistent content creation. Most solo founders either abandon their distribution entirely or post low-effort updates that fail to generate traction.

**The Content Engine** solves the distribution bottleneck. Instead of staring at a blank page every morning, you feed a single core insight—a customer problem, a product milestone, or an operational failure—into a battle-tested repurposing workflow. These twelve prompts transform that single source material into a complete week of platform-native assets: contrarian takes, detailed tactical breakdowns, personal founder reflections, and high-conversion product showcases.

Unlike generic prompt packs that generate fluffy thought leadership, each template is calibrated specifically for early-stage software and service businesses. They enforce structural constraints, remove corporate jargon, and prioritize practical proof points over vague advice. Plug in your raw notes, run the prompts in your AI model of choice, and deploy seven days of brand-building content in under an hour.
includes: 12 structured AI prompts in TXT and Markdown formats
Prompt customization notes and negative constraints
sampleItems: Act as an editorial strategist for a bootstrap founder. I will provide a core operational insight from my business: [INSERT INSIGHT]. Turn this into an analytical breakdown post for LinkedIn. Format: 1 hook sentence questioning standard industry practice, 3 bulleted counter-intuitive observations with real-world examples, and 1 actionable conclusion. Tone: Direct, analytical, zero corporate jargon. Avoid buzzwords like 'game-changer' or 'delve'.

Transform this customer pain point: [INSERT PAIN POINT] into a high-engagement Twitter/X thread starter. Write 3 alternative opening hooks: 1) a punchy contrarian statement, 2) a hard-won lesson learned the expensive way, and 3) a diagnostic question that highlights hidden business costs. Follow each hook with a 2-sentence setup defining the stakes.

items.title: The Contrarian Breakdown
items.body: Act as an editorial strategist for a bootstrap founder. I will provide a core operational insight from my business: [INSERT INSIGHT]. Turn this into an analytical breakdown post for LinkedIn. Format: 1 hook sentence questioning standard industry practice, 3 bulleted counter-intuitive observations with real-world examples, and 1 actionable conclusion. Tone: Direct, analytical, zero corporate jargon. Avoid buzzwords like 'game-changer' or 'delve'.

items.title: The Multi-Angle Thread Hook Generator
items.body: Transform this customer pain point: [INSERT PAIN POINT] into a high-engagement Twitter/X thread starter. Write 3 alternative opening hooks: 1) a punchy contrarian statement, 2) a hard-won lesson learned the expensive way, and 3) a diagnostic question that highlights hidden business costs. Follow each hook with a 2-sentence setup defining the stakes.

items.title: The Step-by-Step Tactical Framework
items.body: Take this operational workflow from my business: [INSERT WORKFLOW]. Convert it into an actionable educational guide for other founders. Structure it into 4 distinct phases: Audit, Setup, Execution, and Maintenance. For each phase, provide one common pitfall and one measurable success metric. Keep sentences short, declarative, and focused strictly on implementation.

items.title: The Failure-to-Feature Story
items.body: Using this mistake or technical setback: [INSERT FAILURE], craft a candid founder reflection post. Structure it using narrative tension: the initial hypothesis, what broke, the quantifiable cost, and the exact system built to fix it permanently. Tone: transparent and pragmatic. Focus on systemic improvements rather than personal sentiment.

items.title: The Pain-First Product Showcase
items.body: I want to highlight this product feature: [INSERT FEATURE]. Write a social post that dedicates 70% of the copy to the costly friction users experience without it, and 30% to how the feature resolves that friction. Frame it around time saved per week. Avoid hyperbole; use concrete operational language suitable for B2B buyers.

items.title: The Curated Resource Matrix
items.body: Based on this domain topic: [INSERT TOPIC], generate a curated resource roundup post. Categorize recommendations into: Essential Tooling, Foundational Reading, and Common Anti-Patterns to Avoid. Include a 1-sentence pragmatic justification for each recommendation based on efficiency and cost for lean teams.

items.title: The Industry Myth Buster
items.body: Analyze this widespread industry assumption: [INSERT ASSUMPTION]. Write a critical deconstruction post showing why this advice damages early-stage startups. Present two comparative operational models: 'What common advice recommends' versus 'What actually scales sustainably'. Conclude with a diagnostic question readers can run on their own business.

items.title: The Weekly Metrics Retrospective
items.body: Take these raw metrics and context: [INSERT METRICS/CONTEXT]. Draft a public building-in-public update. Group the update into three concise sections: Core Growth Metric, Unexpected Bottleneck, and Next Week's Hypothesis. Keep the tone grounded, objective, and analytical, avoiding performative celebration.

items.title: The Mini Case Study Teardown
items.body: Using this brief customer win: [INSERT CUSTOMER RESULT], write a 150-word micro case study. Use the Problem-Intervention-Outcome format. Specify the baseline problem, the single leverage point adjusted, and the final quantified result. End with a one-line lesson applicable to companies in adjacent niches.

items.title: The Decision-Matrix Comparison
items.body: Compare these two industry methodologies or software approaches: [INSERT OPTION A vs OPTION B]. Create a structured decision guide for solo founders. Include: capital efficiency, time-to-value, and technical debt risk for each. Deliver a definitive recommendation based on company maturity stages.

items.title: The Direct Response FAQ Post
items.body: Take this common sales objection: [INSERT OBJECTION]. Write a direct, empathetic social post addressing it head-on without sounding defensive. Explain the structural trade-offs behind our approach, who our solution is NOT for, and who gets maximum ROI from it. Conclude with a clear next step.

items.title: The High-Density Synthesis Newsletter
items.body: Review the core themes explored across these inputs: [PASTE WEEK'S POST TOPICS]. Synthesize them into an executive summary newsletter edition (350 words max). Include an overarching thesis, three key takeaways with actionable bullet points, and one provocative challenge question for the reader's upcoming week.
